newsitem.title: USA: U.S. EPA outlines accord on termite pesticide.
newsitem.headline: U.S. EPA outlines accord on termite pesticide.

text.p: Pesticide manufacturers and formulators have agreed to stop selling air and carpet sprays and pet sprays and shampoos with the insecticide chlorpyrifos, the Environmental Protection Agency said Friday.
Commercial use of chlorpyrifos, mainly manufactured by Dow Chemical Co unit DowElanco, in cracks and crevices will still be allowed, EPA said.
Chlorpyrifos, sold under the trade name Dursban, is one of the most widely used pesticides in the world to control insects, such as termites, in homes. It is also used on farms.
The agreement was designed to limit the exposure of children and pets to the pesticide after it was found to be potentially harmful.
Outlining details of the agreement reached earlier this year, EPA said the sale of air and carpet sprays would be ended and direct application pet products, except pet collars, would be banned.
Marketers of the product would also work with EPA to reduce exposures by getting rid of concentrates that must be mixed in homes and blocking use of the product in toys, drapes and furniture.
The agency has set up a panel to design a study of the potential chronic and neurological effects of the pesticide.
